instructions:
You translate one page of Alexander Grothendieck's handwritten mathematical notes (Montpellier archive) from French
into English. The page is a LaTeX transcription of the manuscript. Some passages are already in English (Grothendieck
wrote parts of these notes in English); keep those exactly as they are.

Write the English version of the whole page, as a faithful raw translation for mathematicians: close to the
wording, keeping Grothendieck's abbreviations, telegraphic style, question marks and hesitations. Do not smooth,
complete, correct or explain anything.

Keep every piece of LaTeX exactly as it is:
- every macro and its arguments' structure: \scanpage{...}, \mspage{...}, \margin{...}, \deleted{...},
  \inserted{...}, \unsure{...}, \illegible{...}, \uline{...}, \diagram{...}, environments, line breaks of displays;
- every formula, symbol and diagram: change no mathematics at all, not even an obvious slip;
- \scanpage and \mspage lines unchanged, in their places.
Translate the French words inside \deleted, \inserted, \margin and \unsure too. An \unsure{a|b} with alternative
readings: translate each alternative and keep the | between them (if two French alternatives give the same English,
still keep both). French words inside \text{...} or \mathrm{...} in formulas: translate them only when they are
ordinary words (e.g. \text{si} -> \text{if}); keep names of objects and notation as they are.
Mathematical terms: use the standard English terms (champ -> stack, catégorie fibrée -> fibred category,
topos, site, faisceau -> sheaf, gerbe -> gerbe, fibration, cofibration, équivalence faible -> weak equivalence,
modèle fermé -> closed model, etc.).

Answer in exactly this form, with nothing before the first marker:
=====BEGIN TARGET_NEW=====
(the complete English page)
=====END TARGET_NEW=====
=====NOTES=====
(readings you were unsure how to translate, with the French; or "none")

=====BEGIN TARGET_NEW=====
Shelfmark 106, scan 6.

\scanpage{6}
\mspage{\unsure{7|3}}
In summary, one finds

\uline{Prop.} For $\Psi:W_{\mathrm{cof}}^{-1}C_{\mathrm{cof}}\longrightarrow W^{-1}C$ to be an equiv. of cat., it is n. and s. that the following condition be satisfied:

$(\unsure{*})$ For \deleted{every} diagram
\diagram{\begin{tikzcd}x \arrow[r,shift left=.65ex,"\varphi"] \arrow[r,shift right=.65ex,"\psi"'] & y \arrow[r,"f","\sim"'] & y'\end{tikzcd}}
where $f\varphi=f\psi$, $f\in W$, $x,y\in C_{\mathrm{cof}}$ \inserted{(whence $[\varphi]=[\psi]$ in $W^{-1}C$)}, one has $[\varphi]=[\psi]$ in $W_{\mathrm{cof}}^{-1}C_{\mathrm{cof}}$.

(condition implied by the condition that $\Psi$ be \uline{faithful})

We shall now work with $C_{\mathrm{cof}}$ instead of $C$. -- thus, changing notation if need be, we shall suppose that ev. object of $C$ is cofibrant.

[\uline{NB} $C_{\mathrm{cof}}$ with the notions induced by $W$ and cof is again a category \unsure{C1 : C3}], the inclusion of $C_{\mathrm{cof}}$ in $C$ commutes with pushouts \deleted{\unsure{which}} associated with diagrams
\diagram{\begin{tikzcd}a \arrow[r,"f"] \arrow[d,"g"'] & b\\ c &\end{tikzcd}}
such that $f$ or $g$ is in cof (the only sums whose existence is postulated!).]

Let, for $x,y$ in $C$,
\[
\uline{\mathrm{Ch}}_0(x,y)=\text{category of diagrams}
\]
\diagram{\begin{tikzcd}x \arrow[dr,"f"'] & y \arrow[d,"i","\sim"']\\ &\bar y\end{tikzcd}}
where $i\in W\cap\mathrm{cof}$ \deleted{\unsure{i.e.}} (\unsure{couniversal weak equiv.}\inserted{if $\mathrm{cof}=\mathrm{cof}_W$}). One defines pairings
\[
\uline{\mathrm{Ch}}_0(x,y)\times\uline{\mathrm{Ch}}_0(y,z)\longrightarrow\uline{\mathrm{Ch}}_0(x,z),\quad (F,G)\longmapsto G\mathbin{\cdot}F
\]
by
\diagram{\begin{tikzcd}
\unsure{x|a} \arrow[dr,"f"',"\deleted{\unsure{\varphi}}"] & y \arrow[d,hook,"i","\sim"'] \arrow[dr,"g"] & z \arrow[d,hook,"j","\sim"']\\
& \bar y \arrow[dr,"g'"',"\text{cocart}"] & \bar z \arrow[d,hook,"\unsure{k}","\sim"']\\
&&\bar z'
\end{tikzcd}}
\deleted{$\unsure{g'f}$}
\[
(g,j)\mathbin{\circ}(f,i)=(\unsure{g'g|g'f})\mathbin{\cdot}\unsure{kj}.
\]
\mspage{5}
